_comment: badlands' temperate PINE forest. Edit and RELAUNCH -- no rebuild. Layers are placed in the order listed and earlier instances block later ones, so the canopy must come first if it is to claim its space before the undergrowth fills in. A `depth` or `density` curve is a trapezoid [rise_start, rise_end, fall_start, fall_end] in METRES of depth-into-forest, and null means 'never falls' (a plateau that runs to the core). `preset` must name a TreeCatalog() entry exactly; a typo fails the load loudly rather than planting the wrong species. `variants` is how many distinct mesh variants to generate (variant 0 keeps the preset's own seed, so it is the tree the model viewer shows).
_tuning_note: There is NO radius_m field: a model's crown radius is MEASURED off the geometry it actually draws (its bark unioned with its LOD0 crown) and instances are spaced so those circles never overlap -- r_i*s_i + r_j*s_j, a sum. So the canopy's density is set by the trees' own size, not by anything in this file, and the load log prints the measured range per layer. What this file still controls: grid_m (how many candidates are TRIED), the density curves and clump noise (which candidates are rolled away), and height_m/scale_range (which, by changing the crown, change the spacing). Keep grid_m WELL BELOW the layer's printed neighbour distance -- at or above it the layer goes roll-limited, the geometry stops deciding anything, and the stand thins for reasons no one can see. Retune by reading the per-layer counts the load log prints.

noise._comment: clump_lo/clump_hi window the clump fBm, which is NOT uniform on [-1,1] -- at 3 octaves it measures mean 0.000, sd 0.354. Read the window against that: the natural-looking [0.35, 0.80] leaves only 4.1% of the map at full density, so it thins the forest evenly instead of carving glades. [0.30, 0.55] gives 40.6% closed canopy against 14.8% true glade. warp_* makes the tree line ragged; without it the boundary is a perfect offset curve of the biome mask.

layers.name: canopy
layers._comment: One species, two statures. Pine (large) is the mature interior stand; Pine (medium) is a different skeleton entirely (not the same tree scaled), so mixing them breaks up the repetition a single preset cannot -- which is what four seed variants each and a wide scale_range are also for. The medium reaches the edge, the large holds the sheltered interior: a stand's tallest trees are the ones that grew up with shelter on every side.

layers.name: sapling
layers._comment: Young pines, thickest in the band just inside the tree line and thinning away under a closed canopy -- which is what the density curve's fall is. They fit in gaps the canopy's own crown circles leave, so their count is a read on how open the stand above them is.

layers.name: bush
layers._comment: Bush 3 is the evergreen and leans interior; Bush 1 and 2 are broadleaf scrub and carry the forest edge. No edge scale ramp -- a bush at the edge is not a younger bush.
